# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

package net.officefloor.hq.app.claim;

/**
 * A claim's status. It starts as DRAFT, is opened (OPEN) and then settled (SETTLED). A clerk's
 * settle above the clerk limit makes it PENDING instead, until a steward approves it (SETTLED) or
 * rejects it (back to OPEN). A DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim can be voided (VOID); a SETTLED one
 * too, by a steward within days of its settlement ({@link VoidClaim}). VOID is final. Only OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count toward any total.
 */
public enum ClaimStatus {
    DRAFT(null), OPEN("CLAIM_OPENED"), PENDING("CLAIM_PENDING"), SETTLED("CLAIM_SETTLED"), VOID("CLAIM_VOIDED");

    private final String auditEvent;

    ClaimStatus(String auditEvent) {
        this.auditEvent = auditEvent;
    }

    /** The audit event written when a claim moves into this status. */
    public String auditEvent() {
        return auditEvent;
    }

    /** Whether a claim in this status may move to {@code next}. */
    public boolean canMoveTo(ClaimStatus next) {
        return switch (next) {
            case OPEN -> this == DRAFT;
            case PENDING -> this == OPEN;
            case SETTLED -> this == OPEN;
            case VOID -> this == DRAFT || this == OPEN || this == PENDING || this == SETTLED;
            case DRAFT -> false;
        };
    }
}
# Settle the selected claims together, in list order, by the rules of settling one. Each that
# cannot be settled is refused and left as it is; the response tells how many were settled (a claim
# sent to PENDING counts) and how many refused.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ValidateBulkSettle
  next: loadSheet
loadSheet:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.LoadSheet
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: settle
# Each claim settled is audited as it is settled: its own line, then the figures it moved.
settle:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.SettleSelectedClaims
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.RespondWithBulkSettle
  govern: [ transaction ]
# Settle a claim. A change its status does not allow is a 409 and writes nothing.
# A viewer may change nothing: refused before anything is read or written.
viewer:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.role.CheckCanChange
  next: loadSheet
loadSheet:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.LoadSheet
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: before
# The sheet's figures before the change, so the rollup lines tell which moved.
before:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.TakeRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: load
load:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.LoadClaim
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: closed
# A claim due by a date inside a closed period is a 409 and writes nothing.
closed:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.period.CheckClaimPeriod
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: apply
apply:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.SettleClaim
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.SaveClaim
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: log
# The status it was saved at, with who, when and its due then.
log:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.LogClaimStatus
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit
# Last before the response: every rule has passed and the change is saved.
audit:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.AuditClaimStatus
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: notify
# After the claim's own line: one line per watcher of its person, once it is settled.
notify:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.watch.NotifyWatchers
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rollup
# After the change's own lines: the figures it moved.
rollup:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.AuditRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.RespondWithClaim
  govern: [ transaction ]

content.text:
Bulk settles are now numbered as batches, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**How it behaves**
- A bulk settle that settles at least one claim (a claim that goes to PENDING counts) takes the sheet's next batch number: 1, 2, and so on. A bulk settle that settles nothing doesn't use up a number.
- Every claim that bulk settle settles gets that number, shown in the claim row's `claim-batch`. A claim settled one at a time shows nothing.
- `bulk-settle-batch` next to the bulk settle button shows the last batch number, or nothing if there hasn't been one. It refreshes along with the claims list after each bulk settle.
- When viewing the sheet as of a past date, both values show as they stood on that date.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V60__settle_batch.sql`, adds a batch counter to the sheet and a `settle_batch` column to claims and to claim history (the history is what the as-of view reads).
- **Server:** `SettleSelectedClaims` takes the batch number when the first claim actually settles and stamps it on each settled claim. `ClaimRepository` saves and reads the column, and gives out batch numbers in a single statement so two bulk settles at once can't share one. Each claim in the claims response now carries its `batch`, and the response also carries the sheet's `lastBatch`.
- **Front end:** the claim row shows `claim-batch` and the bulk settle bar shows `bulk-settle-batch`.

**Choices I made that the request didn't settle (the tests don't cover these):**
- If a steward rejects a PENDING claim that came from a batch, the claim loses its batch number, because it's back to OPEN and no longer settled. If it's approved instead, it keeps the number.
- A claim later settled on its own has its batch number cleared.

Neither choice adds or changes any audit records. Tell me if you'd rather a claim keep its batch number in either case.
